physics.title: The physics of latency
physics.desc: In fiber, light covers 1 km every ~5 µs. Move the distance and compare it with the typical delay of other access technologies.
physics.note: Approximate reference. Fiber propagation is physics (≈ 5 µs/km). Typical access delays (FTTH ~2 ms, cable ~10 ms, 4G ~35 ms) are industry reference values and vary by network.

faq.lead: What people ask us most before signing up.

speed.q: Will I get the advertised speed?
speed.a: Each plan's speed is the maximum delivered to your home, the same down and up. Over a cable you get closest to that maximum; over Wi-Fi it depends on your device, distance and walls. You can measure your current connection with the speed test on this page.

symmetric.a: You upload as fast as you download. Video calls, cloud backups, live streams and big files go up as fast as they come down.

install.q: How much does installation cost and how long does it take?
install.a: A technician brings the fiber to your house or apartment, installs the equipment and leaves everything working.
